A Zener diode with a breakdown voltage of \(8~\text{V}\) and a maximum power dissipation of \(0.5~\text W\) is connected across a potential divider, as shown in the figure, such that the Zener diode experiences the maximum possible voltage. What should be the value of the protective resistance \(R_p\text{?}\)
1.\(172~\Omega\)2.\(192~\Omega\)
3.\(222~\Omega\)4.\(342~\Omega\)
questions.explanation:
Hint:\(P_z=V_z.I_z \) Step 1: Find the voltage across protective resistance. \(20=V_R+V_Z\) \(\Rightarrow 20=V_R+8\) \(\Rightarrow V_R=12\text{ V}\) Step 2: Find the current flowing through Zener diode. \(P_z=V_zI\) \(\Rightarrow 0.5=8I\) \(\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{2}=8I\) \(\Rightarrow I=\dfrac{1}{16}\text{ A}\) Step 3: Find the value of protective resistance. \(V_R=IR\) \(\Rightarrow 12=\dfrac{1}{16}R\) \(\Rightarrow R=192~\Omega\) Hence, option (2) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the DC voltage regulator circuit shown, where the Zener current is \(nI_L\) and the load current is \(I_L,\) what is the value of the series resistor \(R_{s}\text{?}\)
1.\({\dfrac{\left(V_i-V_L\right)}{(n+1) I_L}}\)2.\({\dfrac{\left(V_i+V_L\right)}{(n+1) I_L}}\)
3.\({\dfrac{\left(V_i-V_L\right)}{n I_L}}\)4.\({\dfrac{\left(V_i+V_L\right)}{n I_L}}\)
questions.explanation:
Hint:\(R_s=\frac{\Delta V}{I}\) Step:Find the value of the series resistance\(R_s\). The current flowing through resistance\(R_s\)is given by; \(I_s= (n+1)I_L\) By applying KVL in the circuit, we get; \(V_i = V_s + V_L\) \(\Rightarrow V_s = V_i -V_L\) \(\Rightarrow I_s R_s = V_i -V_L\) \(\Rightarrow R_s = \frac{V_i -V_L}{I_s}\) \(\Rightarrow R_s = \frac{(V_i -V_L)}{(n+1)I_L}\) Hence, option (1) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

 List-IList-II
\(\mathrm{(a)}\)Rectifier\(\mathrm{(i)}\)Used either for stepping up or stepping down the AC voltage.
\(\mathrm{(b)}\)Stabilizer\(\mathrm{(ii)}\)Used to convert AC voltage into DC voltage.
\(\mathrm{(c)}\)Transformer\(\mathrm{(iii)}\)Used to remove any ripple in the rectified output voltage.
\(\mathrm{(d)}\)Filter\(\mathrm{(iv)}\)Used for constant output voltage even when the input voltage or load current changes.

Choose the correct option from the given ones:

1.\(\mathrm{(a)–(ii), (b)–(iv), (c)–(i), (d)–(iii)}\)
2.\(\mathrm{(a)–(iii), (b)–(iv), (c)–(i), (d)–(ii)}\)
3.\(\mathrm{(a)–(ii), (b)–(i), (c)–(iv), (d)–(iii)}\)
4.\(\mathrm{(a)–(ii), (b)–(i), (c)–(iii), (d)–(iv)}\)
questions.explanation:
Hint:Rectifier is used to convert AC to DC. Step: Identify the correct match. (a) Rectifier: A rectifier is an electrical device that converts alternating current (AC), which periodically reverses direction, to direct current (DC), which flows in only one direction. It uses diodes to perform this conversion. (a) Rectifier → (ii) Used to convert AC voltage into DC voltage. (b) Stabilizer:A stabilizer, also known as a voltage regulator, is a device that maintains a constant output voltage even when the input voltage or load current varies. It ensures a stable voltage supply, which is crucial for sensitive electronic equipment. (b) Stabilizer → (iv) Used for constant output voltage even when the input voltage or load current changes. (c) Transformer:A transformer is an electrical device that transfers electrical energy between two or more circuits through electromagnetic induction. It can step up or step down AC voltage levels, depending on the ratio of turns in its primary and secondary coils. (c) Transformer → (i) Used either for stepping up or stepping down the AC voltage. (d) Filter:A filter is a circuit element used to remove unwanted components, such as ripple, from a signal. In the context of rectified output voltage, a filter is often used to smooth out the pulsating DC output obtained from a rectifier, ensuring a more stable and continuous DC voltage. Common types of filters include capacitive filters and inductive filters. (d) Filter → (iii) Used to remove any ripple in the rectified output voltage. Therefore, the correct match is(a)–(ii), (b)–(iv), (c)–(i), (d)–(iii). Hence, option (1) is the correct answer.
